name: Agent Failure Mode Registry
description: A citable registry of the ways autonomous agent systems fail as designed mechanisms, and the conditions under which each failure occurs. Thirty-two families in eight classes, each with builder-checkable trigger conditions, grounding claims bound to verbatim quotes and document hashes, and where one exists, the pre-2020 institutional antecedent documenting the same mechanism in human institutions.
citation: W. A. Kaal, ed., Agent Failure Mode Registry (AFMR) version 1.0, 2026-07-30. https://wulfkaal.github.io/afmr/

identifier_policy.stability: Identifiers are permanent. A family is never renumbered and never reused. A family withdrawn from use is marked deprecated and retained.

grounding.verification: sha256 over raw PDF bytes of the source work

families.name: Sybil and Identity Multiplication
families.definition: One party operates many apparent agents, defeating any assumption the design makes per identity.
trigger_conditions: Creating an additional agent identity costs less than the influence one identity carries
Any quorum, sampling, average, or one-vote-per-identity rule is in use
No proof of distinctness is required at registration

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: domain specific issuance per competence tag

families.name: Identity Discontinuity and Whitewashing
families.definition: An agent abandons a degraded identity and resumes with a clean one, so history stops constraining behavior.
trigger_conditions: Identity creation is costless or near costless
Standing is not portable to a new identity and history is not retained on exit
The population is pseudonymous or unattested

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: actors accept known problems to protect standing, which presumes standing persists

families.name: Cold Start and Bootstrapping
families.definition: The design requires accumulated standing, participants, or history that it provides no way to acquire.
trigger_conditions: Participation requires staking standing the new entrant cannot yet have earned
Initial population is zero or below the quorum the mechanism assumes
No provisional, sponsored, or probationary entry path exists

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: entry problem where adjudication requires staking reputation one does not yet hold

families.name: Standing Transferability Defect
families.definition: Standing can be bought, sold, delegated, or pooled, so it stops measuring the performance it was meant to represent.
trigger_conditions: The standing instrument is fungible or transferable between identities
Capital and earned standing are staked in the same act
Delegation moves standing rather than only voice

families.name: Staking and Incentive Misalignment
families.definition: What an agent risks diverges from what the system needs it to care about.
trigger_conditions: The stake is smaller than the value at issue in a single decision
Loss from a bad outcome falls on a party other than the decider
Stake is denominated in something the agent can reacquire faster than it can be slashed

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: actors capture upside of excessive risk without bearing all of its cost

families.name: Missing Reward Channel
families.definition: An action surface exists with no reward attached, so rational agents will not allocate compute to it.
trigger_conditions: The behavior the system needs is not on any reward path
Agents are economically rational over standing or utility flows
Contribution and selection are rewarded asymmetrically

families.name: Plutocratic Capture
families.definition: Influence tracks holdings rather than earned standing, so the largest holders determine outcomes.
trigger_conditions: Weight is a function of balance, stake size, or compute rather than validated performance
Holdings are acquirable on an open market
No cap, curve, or quadratic dampening applies to concentration

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: instrument design changing whose interests a decider serves

families.name: Moral Hazard and Backstop Expectation
families.definition: An expectation of rescue, retry, or rollback changes risk taking before any rescue occurs.
trigger_conditions: Failed actions can be retried at no cost to standing
A human or protocol operator is expected to reverse bad outcomes
Slashing is discretionary rather than automatic

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: limited liability as a driver of excessive risk taking

families.name: Specification Incompleteness
families.definition: The principal cannot enumerate every action and inaction in advance, so the agent's mandate is necessarily underspecified.
trigger_conditions: The action space is open ended or tool mediated
The agent operates without per-action approval
The instruction set is stated as goals rather than as permitted operations

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: bounded rationality and incomplete foresight make complete contracting over agent action impossible

families.name: Reward Hacking and Proxy Capture
families.definition: The agent raises the measured objective without producing the outcome the objective stood for.
trigger_conditions: The objective is a learned or aggregated proxy rather than the outcome itself
The agent can observe and iterate against the measure
No held-out or adversarial check is applied to the measure

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: reputational and market proxies standing in for direct incentives

families.name: Metric Capture and Measurement Failure
families.definition: The chosen metric ceases to track the property it stands for once it becomes the target.
trigger_conditions: Standing or reward is computed from a single scalar
The metric is disclosed to the parties it scores
No periodic revalidation of the metric against outcomes occurs

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: market pricing of governance change as a proxy for governance quality

families.name: Definitional Ambiguity in Machine Applied Rules
families.definition: A term carrying operational weight has no settled boundary, so automated application produces outcomes no party intended.
trigger_conditions: Rules are applied by code without a human interpretive layer
Terms are inherited from natural language instruments
No authority is named to settle meaning when application is contested

families.name: Oversight Capacity Gap
families.definition: Agent behavior exceeds the resources, expertise, or access of whoever is nominally supervising it.
trigger_conditions: Action volume exceeds what the supervisor can sample meaningfully
The supervisor lacks access to the agent's inputs or intermediate reasoning
Supervision is assigned but not resourced

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: monitoring capacity as the binding constraint on oversight

families.name: Oversight Latency
families.definition: Review is slower than action, so by the time a judgment lands the state it judged is gone.
trigger_conditions: Agent action rate exceeds adjudication rate
Actions are not reversible after the review window
Review is batched or scheduled rather than gating

families.name: Alignment Tax and Exogenous Constraint Scaling
families.definition: External control scales against capability, so oversight cost rises faster than the capability it constrains.
trigger_conditions: Alignment relies on constraint imposed from outside the agent's incentive structure
Agent capability is expected to increase
No endogenous stake grows with capability

families.name: Absent Human Backstop
families.definition: No human authority can halt, reverse, or reinterpret automated execution, so cryptographic or procedural correctness substitutes for trust and fails to produce it.
trigger_conditions: No named party can halt execution
No escalation path exists from automated outcome to human judgment
Human interpretation is not stated to prevail where the two diverge

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: without a decentralized human backstop to code, cryptographic security does not create trust between principals and agents

families.name: Feedback Degradation Above Evaluator Capability
families.definition: Human or agent evaluation degrades precisely where the evaluated system is hardest to evaluate, including where it exceeds the evaluator.
trigger_conditions: Evaluators score outputs they cannot independently verify
The evaluated system is at or above evaluator capability in the domain
Evaluator agreement is used as the quality signal

families.name: Unstaked Adjudication
families.definition: Whoever judges a contribution risks nothing on the judgment, so judgment is cheap and drifts.
trigger_conditions: Validators or reviewers stake nothing on their verdict
Verdicts are not contestable within a stated window
No standing consequence follows from a verdict later shown wrong

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: consequence attaching to the adjudicating party as the source of care

families.name: Training and Annotation Bias Propagation
families.definition: Bias in annotators or automated labeling propagates into the model and then into every decision the agent makes.
trigger_conditions: Labels are produced by a narrow annotator pool or by another model
No demographic or scenario stratification is checked
Label provenance is not recorded

families.name: Human Judgment Displacement
families.definition: Automation replaces judgment in a setting that required judgment, and the loss is not detected because the output still looks well formed.
trigger_conditions: Output is fluent and confident regardless of correctness
No sampled human review of accepted outputs occurs
The prior human process left no record to compare against

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: decision makers relying on presumptively optimal rules for want of decentralized information

families.name: Mutual Audit Capture
families.definition: Agents assigned to oversee one another converge on mutual approval, so peer monitoring devolves into self serving behavior.
trigger_conditions: Agents both audit and are audited by the same population
No anti collusion constraint or randomized assignment applies
Approval is cheaper for the auditor than refusal

families.name: Collusion Rings and Reciprocal Validation
families.definition: A subset of agents validates one another to manufacture standing, and formal mechanism design alone does not detect it.
trigger_conditions: Validation is reciprocal or citation-like
One party can field several competing agents per task
No ring detection or downranking of reciprocal patterns is applied

families.name: Collective Action and Coordination Failure
families.definition: Individually rational agent behavior produces a collectively worse outcome and no mechanism reconciles the two.
trigger_conditions: Payoff to defection exceeds payoff to cooperation in a single interaction
Interactions are not expected to repeat, or identity does not persist across them
No mechanism prices the externality

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: private parties acting on decentralized information without a reconciling mechanism

families.name: Delegation Opportunism
families.definition: An agent acting for a principal, or for another agent, captures private benefit at the principal's expense, and monitoring costs more than it recovers.
trigger_conditions: The delegation chain is more than one link deep
The principal cannot observe intermediate actions
The agent's objective is not identical to the principal's

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: agency conflicts from separation of ownership and control cannot be fully addressed because monitoring is costly

families.name: Oracle and Input Corruption
families.definition: The mechanism executes correctly on an input that is wrong, stale, manipulated, or injected.
trigger_conditions: Any input crosses a trust boundary without attestation
A single source can determine an input value
No staleness bound or sanity range is enforced

families.name: Automated Execution Rigidity
families.definition: Execution cannot accommodate circumstances the code did not anticipate, and cannot be amended in time to matter.
trigger_conditions: Execution is irreversible once triggered
Amendment requires a process slower than the harm
No circuit breaker or pause authority exists

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: rules are adaptable only where the process producing them integrates dynamic elements

families.name: Code Defect Exploitation
families.definition: A defect in deployed code is exercised by an adversary before it is found by its authors.
trigger_conditions: Code holds value or authority and is publicly reachable
No independent audit or adversarial review preceded deployment
Upgrade path is absent or itself unguarded

families.name: Custody and Key Compromise
families.definition: Control of an agent's identity, assets, or authority is lost or captured through key or custody failure.
trigger_conditions: An agent holds signing authority without threshold or rotation
Key material is reachable by the same process that uses it
No recovery path distinguishes loss from theft

families.name: Recentralization Drift
families.definition: A system designed to distribute authority concentrates it again through tooling, delegation, capital, or expertise asymmetry.
trigger_conditions: A small number of operators run most infrastructure or most agents
Delegation is permitted and defaults are sticky
Participation cost rises with system maturity

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: concentration of institution specific information in few hands

families.name: Rule Obsolescence and Ossification
families.definition: A rule persists after the conditions that justified it have changed, and resists revision.
trigger_conditions: Amendment requires a supermajority of a population that has stopped participating
No scheduled review of parameters against outcomes exists
Parameters were set once at launch

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: adaptability requires dynamic elements in the rulemaking process itself

families.name: Participation Collapse
families.definition: Eligible participants stop participating, leaving decisions to a small, self selected, or unrepresentative remainder.
trigger_conditions: Participation is unrewarded or costs more than it returns
Quorum is defined against eligible rather than active population
Decision volume exceeds attention available

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: board independence contingent on who actually exercises the function

families.name: Enforcement and Liability Gap
families.definition: A rule exists and cannot be enforced, or no recognized person bears the obligation, so liability has nowhere to attach.
trigger_conditions: No legal person is identifiable behind the agent
The obligated party is outside the reach of any enforcing authority
Sanction depends on a party that can exit at will

institutional_antecedent.mechanism: procedural correctness failing to substitute for an accountable party
